ian: quick thread — ran into a weird divergence between our replay and synthetic SLO runs. replay p95 ~120ms p99 ~420ms, synthetic sim with loadgen (poisson) p95 ~90ms p99 ~260ms. wondering if this is kernel selection + kv-warmup or our synthetic generator being too 'nice'.

priya: do you have the seq-len and prefix cache hit rates for the replay? replay tends to have long-tail prefixes which hurt KV efficiency.

ian: good call. replay seq-dist: 70% short (<64), 25% mid (64-512), 5% long (>512). kv cache hit: 0.58 overall but drops to 0.21 for long prefixes.

samir: that distribution will flip kernel choices at inference time. our heuristic picks grouped attention kernel for long tokens which has worse startup latencies. microbatching interacts too — when batchwidth==1 we lose kernel amortization.

anya: +1. also check microbatch sizing: I saw p99 jump when microbatch went from 4 -> 1 in the repro. If your synthetic generator always packs to microbatch=4 you'll look better than replay. :thinking_face:

ci-bot: nightly/sim-run completed: model=rw-13b-quant, hw=A100-40GB, synthetic-poisson qps=1200, microbatch=4, batch-buffer=32, p95=88ms, p99=265ms, 95th-cost-token=$0.000012

priya: do we have a step-by-step for the replay? are we preserving client-side pacing and think time? naive replay can overpack requests (burstiness) or underpack (empty gaps) depending on how arrival times are generated.

ian: replay is from prod traces but we normalized per-user interarrival to preserve relative pauses. we did not simulate client rtt jitter. we replayed with the same absolute timestamps into the test cluster.

samir: absolute replay into an isolated test box will change microbatching behavior because buffer timeouts and internal batching windows interact with arrival spacing. synthetic poisson isn't capturing burstiness either.

kevin: idea: run a controlled hybrid: take replay arrival timestamps but randomize prefix order to vary seq-len mixing, and run with both warm and cold KV cache (evict between runs). compare kernel traces.

priya: also instrument kernel selection logs. we should dump a small CSV: ts,kernel,seq_len,batchwidth,kv_hit for each call for 10k calls. that'll show correlation.

ian: trying that now. sample kernel log snippet: ```2026-03-17T16:05:12Z INFO kernel_select model=rw-13b kernel=grouped_attention seq=768 batch=2 kv_hit=false```

anya: for p95/p99 I prefer blocking on tail-sampling: run many short runs with different seeds and bootstrap percentiles rather than a single long run. single-run p99 is fragile with outliers.

samir: agreed. plus we need to report effective concurrency and microbatch occupancy distribution (histogram). p99 alone without occupancy is useless.

ci-bot: replay-hybrid job queued: job_id=hybrid-176303-1, config={preserve_arrivals:true, randomize_prefix_order:true, kv_warmup:true, runs:20}

kevin: one experimental note — kernel switch costs are asymmetric. switching from fwd-optimized->grouped at runtime causes a ~6-8ms penalty on first token due to different kernel init paths. if replay causes more switches, tails spike.

priya: propose checklist for any SLO run: 1) publish seq-len distribution; 2) publish microbatch occupancy histogram; 3) publish kv-hit time-series; 4) kernel-switch events count; 5) run N short seeds and bootstrap p95/p99.

ian: love it. will run hybrid job and post results + csvs. question for you all: how much should we weight replay vs synthetic when gating a perf regression? my gut says replay > synthetic for customer impact but synthetic for root-cause isolation.

anya: exactly that. replay = fidelity (impact), synthetic = signal (isolate). use both with the checklist. also add a 'stress' synthetic mode that pushes worst-case seq-len mixes to validate fallbacks.

samir: and add kernel-switch unit tests in CI that assert cost delta < X ms per switch to catch accidental regressions in init path.

ian: ok thanks. will upload hybrid-run logs and attach kernel csv. follow-ups: @priya can you propose bootstrapping script? @kevin can you list kernel init optimizations to try if we confirm switch penalty?

priya: on it, will draft a small bootstrap util (python) and share tomorrow.

kevin: will audit init paths and see what we can pre-warm or lazy-initialize differently.

ian: great — closing for now, will ping again with concrete numbers. :rocket:
